decisionRules.because: NVIDIA documentation states that MAISI is a three-dimensional latent diffusion model that generates high-resolution synthetic CT images with or without anatomical annotations, produces paired segmentation masks, supports outputs up to 512×512×768 voxels, supports variable voxel sizes, can annotate up to 127 anatomical classes, and allows controllable anatomy size for ten specific classes.
decisionRules.when: Need synthetic 3D CT volume generation with paired segmentation masks and controllable anatomy or voxel settings.

decisionRules.because: The arXiv technical report states that BMC-CLIPCF outperforms PMC-CLIP on all evaluated tasks, outperforms BioMed-CLIP in 8 out of 10 general biomedical imaging classification subsets, improves zero-shot classification by an average of 6.56%, and attains stronger image-text retrieval while using less compute. These are upstream BMC-CLIPCF claims, not directly verified Forge-wrapper runtime benchmarks.
decisionRules.when: Need biomedical image-text representation learning use cases such as similarity, retrieval, or zero-shot classification, and upstream checkpoint evidence is sufficient.

decisionRules.because: The findings support different task families and modalities for the two candidates: BMC-CLIPCF is evidenced as a biomedical vision-language model, while MAISI is evidenced as a 3D CT generation NIM. decisionRules.because: The findings do not specify the exact Forge-wrapper evaluation protocol for biomedica-bmc-clip-cf, and they also do not specify MAISI segmentation label mappings or returned mask encoding. decisionRules.when: Need a deployment choice driven by exact wrapper/runtime protocol details, such as BMC-CLIPCF prompt templates, pooling, normalization, or MAISI label-map and mask-encoding details.

supports: BMC-CLIP is a suite of CLIP-style models continuously pre-trained on the BIOMEDICA dataset via streaming.
BMC-CLIP models achieve state-of-the-art performance across 40 biomedical imaging tasks.
BMC-CLIP improves zero-shot classification by an average of 6.56%, with named subset improvements.
BMC-CLIP attains stronger image-text retrieval while using less compute than prior models.
Concept filtering yields better average performance than concept balancing and full-dataset pretraining for zero-shot classification and retrieval.
BMC-CLIPCF outperforms PMC-CLIP on all evaluated tasks and outperforms BioMed-CLIP in 8 out of 10 general biomedical imaging classification subsets.
The combined BIOMEDICA dataset used for BMC-CLIP contains 10,277 volumes across 40 biomedical imaging domains.

supports: MAISI is a three-dimensional latent diffusion model that generates high-resolution synthetic CT images with or without anatomical annotations.
MAISI is intended for data augmentation and creating realistic medical imaging data to mitigate privacy concerns or rare-condition scarcity.
MAISI release 1.0.1 replaces the DDPM noise scheduler with Rectified Flow and is described as faster than version 1.0.0.
MAISI generates 3D CT volumes up to 512×512×768 voxels.
MAISI supports variable voxel sizes from 0.5 mm to 5.0 mm.
MAISI can annotate up to 127 anatomical classes.
MAISI allows controllable anatomy size for ten specific classes.
MAISI produces paired segmentation masks alongside generated CT images.
Release 1.0.1 adds better support for head region and small output volumes compared with version 1.0.0.

dossier.taskDefinition: This group covers selection between exactly two Forge candidates with different medical-imaging task families: (1) biomedica-bmc-clip-cf for biomedical image-text embedding, similarity, retrieval, and zero-shot classification claims supported only as upstream BMC-CLIPCF checkpoint evidence; and (2) nvidia-maisi-nim for controllable generation of synthetic 3D CT volumes with paired segmentation masks through the NVIDIA MAISI NIM runtime. Out of scope are direct cross-modality numeric comparisons between these candidates, clinical diagnosis or treatment use, non-CT generative imaging, and any claim that depends on an unverified downstream head, prompt template, pooling rule, preprocessing pipeline, adapter, or service behavior not directly specified in the cited primary sources.
